jess (Acme): Hey team, we're getting intermittent 429s + big latency spikes. Happening when we fan out a prefetch path to two model variants (rwd-32k + rwd-64k). Not consistent but correlates with short bursts. logs + curl below. Anyone seen this pattern?

alexa (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste one example request id + the curl you used? Also are you doing prefetch to both variants in parallel or sequentially? And roughly what QPS/concurrency are you driving?

jess (Acme): Repro: bursty prefetcher: ~10 sustained qps but bursts up to ~45 concurrent prefetches for 10s. Each prefetch includes ~28k context tokens (user history) + ~1k prompt. Using: POST /v1/chat/completions -> model=rwd-64k or rwd-32k depending on user. Sample curl: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"rwd-64k","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"..."},{"role":"user","content":"<28k tokens context>"}],"max_tokens":512}' -w "\nstatus:%{http_code}\n" -o /tmp/resp.json```
Request id in header: X-Request-Id: ab12c3d4

michael (sre): Also seeing 429s in backend traces: `{"error":"rate_limit","reason":"per_model_rpm_exceeded","model":"rwd-64k"}`. Timestamps line up with the 10s bursts.

alexa (support): This fits per-model RPM/TPM enforcement + concurrency smoothing. Quick overview: each model variant enforces its own request-per-minute (RPM) and tokens-per-minute (TPM) budget; a single fanout that hits two variants counts separately against each variant's RPM/TPM. Large context length increases token accounting (context + prompt + response tokens). Also we apply soft concurrency caps to avoid overloading long-context sessions.

alexa (support): Rough numbers (for this tenant class): rwd-32k: ~600 RPM, 180k TPM, max concurrency ~12; rwd-64k: ~400 RPM, 240k TPM, max concurrency ~8. These are approximate but explain why 45 parallel prefetches can blow past per-model RPM quickly, especially if some requests go to the 64k variant.

ivan (infra): Extra nuance — prefetch paths often fanout multiple variants (fallbacks) which multiplies RPM. If you prefetch N variants in parallel, you effectively multiply request rate by N. Also our token accounting counts the entire context at request time even if the response is short.

jess (Acme): That makes sense. We have a fallback strategy that prefetches both 32k + 64k simultaneously to see which returns first. Looks dumb in hindsight. Is there a way to keep fast fallback without doubling rate?

alexa (support): Recommendations: 1) Switch to sequential fallback with a short hedged delay (e.g., send to primary, after 150-300ms send to fallback only if no progress). 2) Add jitter/poisson spacing on prefetch bursts. 3) Reduce parallel prefetch concurrency (cap to 8-10). 4) Consolidate context where possible (trim unused history). 5) If you need sustained high burst capacity, ask about Dedicated capacity or per-model limit increases — we can provision higher RPM/TPM for your org.

alexa (support): Quick repro steps for us to reproduce: 1) Run a short script that fires 45 concurrent requests split 60/40 between rwd-32k and rwd-64k, each with ~28k context, 512 max_tokens, for 20s. Include X-Request-Id and org header. 2) Capture response headers, especially x-rwd-ratelimit-* and x-request-id. 3) Provide at least one response.json and trace link. Example script: ```bash
for i in $(seq 1 45); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-64k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<28k tokens>"}],"max_tokens":512}' &
done
wait
```

michael (sre): When you run that, include `?debug=ratelimit` on the request if possible so our infra will log the exact quota key hit. Also include timestamps to match traces.

alexa (support): Immediate short-term mitigation you can try before infra changes: disable parallel prefetch to both variants, change to a single prefered variant (even if slightly slower) to avoid doubling RPM, and implement 429 retry with exponential backoff + jitter. Example backoff: retry after 500ms -> 1s -> 2s with jitter and cap at 3 retries. :thumbsup:

jess (Acme): Okay we'll toggle prefetch to sequential + add backoff and run the repro. If we still need throughput we'll open a Dedicated request. Thanks!
